title: Data on Cases of Anti-social Behaviours in Public Places and Penalties or Prevention Measures Introduced
what_it_is: Data on Cases of Anti-social Behaviours in Public Places and Penalties or Prevention Measures Introduced

sections.label: Police do not track anti-social behaviour
sections.summary: Police do not track anti-social behaviour cases; NEA investigates public urination, with fines up to $1,000, unless criminal conduct is disclosed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Police do not track cases of anti-social behaviour.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For example, for cases of public urination, in the absence of factors indicating criminal conduct, the National Environment Agency (NEA) will investigate and take action.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Offenders are liable under the Environmental Public Health (Public Cleansing) Regulations to a maximum fine of $1,000 for the first conviction.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Police may investigate such cases if a criminal offence is disclosed.

sections.label: Whole-of-society approach to deterrence
sections.summary: Deterring anti-social behaviour needs a whole-of-society approach, with Government education and enforcement, and NEA working with stakeholders on public urination.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Deterring anti-social behaviour requires a whole-of-society approach, with the Government playing a part through education and enforcement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In the case of public urination, NEA adopts a firm enforcement approach and also works with stakeholders such as community leaders, Town Councils and schools to foster social responsibility towards keeping public spaces clean.
